findings.title: User action needed · Retrieve a known preference
findings.observed: During the 0.2.102 voice test, Samantha queried the Ledger and then said she had no saved site profile, although an active site-scoped preference already existed.
findings.recommendation: When a preference is relevant to a choice, recall its active scope and rule automatically and apply it without asking the user to name Context Ledger.
findings.verification: Spoken retest: Ledger returned the saved preference without being named; Samantha acted and the user independently confirmed seeing the expected Netflix profile.

details.Source review: The existing ledger_task supports recall, preference, lookup, and capture. The PR adds proactive recall guidance; source review did not identify a missing tool capability.
details.Source verification: The system prompt says to call ledger_task proactively before preference-sensitive choices. The preference helper test saves and recalls an exact scope+rule without calling the helper model.
details.Privacy boundary: The owner-authorized investigation read saved Ledger records. Preference values, decision identifiers, original prompts and raw session content are omitted from this public report; source tests use synthetic data.
details.Latest live evidence: Snapshot fa5e86a5233cda2010525b0494fff1dd2eb9d455112a2277549f809ae532d2e5, session sref_3be882a84bf77eafe3dc0becd04d5057: two ledger lookup operations succeeded. Query and result content are not captured, so preference relevance remains unknown.
details.User action: When prompted, ask Samantha to use a specific preference that you know has already been saved, without telling her to consult Context Ledger. This is needed to compare the expected preference with the recalled and applied result.
details.Root-cause evidence: Samantha generic lookup constructs caller_scope with an empty tools list. Ledger find filters records by permitted scopes, so generic lookup without a tool scope cannot retrieve a tool-scoped preference. The exact live lookup arguments were not captured, so this explains a reproducible path, not the full live cause.
details.Candidate fix: ACU 0.2.102 candidate passes an explicitly supplied site or app scope through generic lookup and instructs the model to provide it. Focused source tests passed. Whether Samantha supplies the correct scope automatically and applies the saved choice remains unverified until an installed voice test.
details.Installed candidate: ACU 0.2.102 was built, signed, notarized and installed from PR commit 98563a4. Thirty-three installed-package simulated Ledger tests passed; the voice gate did not prove a spoken interaction, so automatic scope choice and application are still unverified.
details.Controlled follow-up: The 0.2.102 helper was exercised against the actual Ledger with a bounded selection stub: the same lookup without site scope returned zero records, while a site-scoped lookup returned two. The scoped path can read the existing records; the actual live request scope is unknown.
details.Lookup audit: The Ledger access audit recorded a concrete query naming the site and profile choice and returned zero results at the exact time of the voice lookup. It does not retain the request scope, so the reason that specific lookup missed the record is still unproven.
details.Latest test: The session record shows an initial profile question, then an explicit request to use saved preferences, followed by a zero-match recall. The owner named the choice; Samantha reported selecting it. No independent page readback was captured.
details.Scope discrepancy: A newly saved preference from that session was independently read back under the browser tool scope; earlier matching decisions were saved under the site tool scope. The failed recall scope and rule were not retained, so the precise reason for the miss is not proven. Personal values and identifiers are omitted.
details.Root cause analysis: The voice-facing Live instructions allow brief clarifications to be answered directly; the proactive Ledger instruction lives in the backend instructions and does not guarantee backend delegation at a preference-sensitive choice. Exact-scope and exact-rule recall is brittle: controlled reads found saved decisions with their precise scope and rule, but equivalent site identifiers or a different rule returned none. The actual live recall scope and rule were not recorded, so its specific mismatch is unknown.
details.Required fix: Ensure preference-sensitive choices reach the backend before asking; resolve site identity independently of browser tool, search existing scoped decisions without guessing a rule, and apply only an unambiguous active match. Record bounded scope/rule and delegation metadata to diagnose misses, without recording private values. Verify save, recall and application on an installed build.
details.Fix plan: The existing PR #87 implementation plan now includes a scoped automatic-preference milestone, known limits, failure handling, privacy boundaries, owner paths and installed acceptance checks. Legacy browser-scope migration and the voice decision-boundary signal remain open design decisions.
details.0.2.103 candidate: Adds explicit voice delegation guidance and a bounded same-scope candidate search when an exact rule misses. Candidates require disambiguation and do not establish a saved preference by themselves. Site alias resolution, deterministic voice routing, conflict handling and live acceptance remain open.

findings.observed: Durable preferences and important decisions should be captured when they are stated, then reused at the right time without reminders.
findings.recommendation: Capture durable preferences in their exact scope and rule. Use the decision capture path for critical decisions, and confirm a save only after the ledger returns a receipt.
findings.verification: Typed synthetic live test passed: Samantha saved a scoped preference, updated it and recalled the updated value; independent Ledger readback confirmed replacement. User-authored spoken capture and critical-decision behavior were not tested.

details.Source change: The PR adds guidance for proactive preference capture and retrieval through the existing ledger_task tool.
details.Supersession rule: Updating a preference supersedes only an active user_decision with the same exact scope and rule. General captures do not auto-supersede; the current tool does not create an explicit supersedes link.
details.Source verification: Preference writes include exact scope+rule and return `saved` only with a decision ID. Critical capture checks require durable/model-safe status, a user quote, future trigger, changed choice, and receipt.

details.Supersession behavior: Context Ledger's same-scope+rule user_decision behavior is the intended preference supersession path. General captures are explicitly not treated as superseding.
